item.description:
A newborn who suffered burns to several parts of the body from excessive heat at the neonatal intensive care unit (NICU) of Royal Care and Surgical Hospital in Dhaka’s Chankharpul has died, four days after the incident.
The baby died on Wednesday afternoon while on life support at the NICU of Dhaka Medical College Hospital (DMCH), where the child had been receiving treatment. DMCH police camp in-charge Inspector Md Habibur Rahman said the body had been kept in the hospital morgue.
The baby was born at DMCH early on November 7. Doctors advised NICU care, but as no beds were available there, the family took the newborn to Royal Care and Surgical Hospital on the advice of a man named Matiur.
The baby’s father, Golam Rabbani, alleged that shortly after admission to the private hospital’s NICU, excessive heat burned parts of the child’s head, back and legs. He said the family heard screams inside the hospital and learned that the baby had been burned. He also alleged that no one was available when they went inside to check.
Rabbani said the baby was rescued and taken to the National Institute of Burn and Plastic Surgery, which later referred the child to DMCH. The newborn was admitted to the hospital’s NICU and kept on life support, but died as the condition deteriorated on Wednesday afternoon.

item.title: BNP on high alert amid talk of Hasina’s December return
item.description:
What the month of December holds has been a major topic of discussion in the country's politics over the past several months, ever since ousted former prime minister Sheikh Hasina, who has now spent over two years in India, announced her intention to return to Bangladesh that month.
Leaders and activists of the Awami League, which remains under a ban on its activities, have been energized by Hasina's announcement, and they have been campaigning on social media, as well as through their foreign networks, to prepare the grounds for her return, which remains uncertain.
The ruling Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP) believes the Awami League’s underground network is trying to stoke unrest across the country in anticipation of welcoming back their leader, with government sources saying the party is planning subversive activities.
The BNP has stepped up organizational activities, mobilized its grassroots leaders and activists, and sought to mend ties with former allies. It has also instructed its leaders and workers to remain alert, avoid provocation and report suspicious activities to the administration rather than take the law into their own hands.
The party and its affiliated organizations, including Jubo Dal, Chhatra Dal (JCD) and Sramik Dal, are active on the ground. Law enforcement agencies suspect AL activists were involved in recent garment workers’ protests, cocktail explosions and vehicle arson in Dhaka and other parts of the country.
At a BNP parliamentary party meeting chaired by Prime Minister and BNP Chairman Tarique Rahman at parliament premises on Monday, “The message is loud and clear: we are on the streets, and we must remain on the streets. All conspiracies must be confronted on the streets,” Tarique told the meeting.
Meanwhile, Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed said the government would use the Bangladesh-India extradition treaty to bring Hasina back.
The home minister assured parliament that no conspiracy, whether hatched inside or outside the country, would be allowed to revive fascism.
“I want to assure the people of the country that no conspiracy or blueprint, whether hatched within the country, beyond the border or through a combination of forces, will be allowed to be implemented here,” he said.
Referring to a cocktail explosion on the roof of a car near the Dhaka University Business Faculty building, Salahuddin said such an incident did not mean that the country's law and order situation had deteriorated. It was not reasonable, he said, to describe the overall situation as extremely alarming based on a few symbolic incidents.
State Minister for Foreign Affairs Humaiun Kobir said Hasina could not return on a new passport and that her return would have to follow the legal process under the extradition treaty.
Political analysts say the BNP faces the challenge of rebuilding its organizational structure while running the government. After being out of power for a long time, some leaders are now occupied with government and administrative responsibilities. Competition for local leadership, dissatisfaction over committee positions and concerns about discipline have also emerged.
The party is preparing for its national council and reorganizing its central committee, standing committee, advisory council and affiliate organizations. New committees have recently been announced for BNP's Dhaka North and South units and Jubo Dal's Dhaka North unit. Reorganization of Chhatra Dal, Jubo Dal and Swechchhasebak Dal is also underway.
BNP Acting Secretary General Ruhul Kabir Rizvi said people would never accept Hasina's return in the way AL leaders were claiming.
“Will she suddenly descend by parachute and everyone will welcome her by beating drums? Can that ever happen? The soil of Bengal is the soil of heroes. This land has given birth to many heroes. Those who flee the country after shedding the blood of their own people cannot simply fly back and take over. That is never possible. The people themselves will resist Hasina,” he said.
“In that roar, neither Sheikh Hasina nor even her patrons and their grandfathers will be able to do anything,” Rizvi added, saying people always resist injustice.
“The streets and the field of movements have not been given to anyone as hereditary property, allowing you to provoke us one after another while we sit silently,” he said.
“You can see that cocktails and bombs are being exploded from inside alleys in some places. Instructions are reportedly coming from a neighboring country. The people will resist them appropriately. The government is always prepared in this regard,” he said.
BNP standing committee member Amanullah Aman said the public would not accept attempts to create unrest through a few cocktail explosions. Anti-fascist political parties would jointly resist any move to bring back the ousted autocrat, he said.
“She can come, let her come. The people of Bangladesh are also prepared,” Aman said.
State Minister for Expatriates' Welfare and Overseas Employment Nurul Haque Nur, also the president of Gono Odhikar Parishad, which is a BNP ally, described the talk of Hasina's return in December as ridiculous, alleging that hostile foreign forces were using fascist elements to create instability in Bangladesh.
BNP National Executive Committee member Mamun Hasan said the party would remain active on the ground but would not allow disorder. It would cooperate with the government and administration to maintain peace and resist anyone attempting to create unrest.
“As the party in government, we will do whatever is necessary to cooperate with the administration if such cooperation is needed,” he told UNB.
Another BNP National Executive Committee member, Akramul Hasan, said the party would organize resistance against any terrorist activities. He said the AL should seek forgiveness first from the people if it wanted to return to politics.
He said cocktail explosions might create some fear in a city as large as Dhaka but would have no meaningful political impact. Referring to the AL's past record of arson, deaths, corruption, looting, misrule, crossfire and enforced disappearances, he said isolated acts of violence would not win public support.
JCD President Rakibul Islam Rakib said attempts to create disorder in the country are worsening the situation for AL's jailed leaders and activists, he said.
Dismissing the December return claims, Rakib said Bangladesh would celebrate the month of victory in the Liberation War in the grandest manner since 1971. Chhatra Dal will organize Victory celebrations at educational institutions across the country from December 1.
Meanwhile, the BNP is taking initiatives to reduce some of the distance that has opened up between itself and its allies. Some partner parties have expressed dissatisfaction over political assessments after the formation of the government, pre-election commitments and the pace of state reforms.
The BNP plans to hold meetings with its partners in late November or early December. Discussions may also take place with Tarique Rahman on the party's 31-point reform proposal, the July Charter, constitutional amendments, local government elections and future political programs.

item.title: Tarique exchanges greetings with world leaders at COP31
item.description:
Prime Minister Tarique Rahman exchanged greetings and pleasantries with heads of state and government and senior representatives of international organisations at the Leaders’ Lounge ahead of the opening ceremony of the World Leaders’ Summit of the 31st UN Climate Change Conference (COP31) in Türkiye’s Antalya on Wednesday.
The prime minister reached the venue of the United Nations Climate Change Conference at 10:10am local time, where he was welcomed by the organisers, said PM’s Deputy Press Secretary Hasan Shiplu.
His wife, Dr Zubaida Rahman, accompanied him. Foreign Minister Dr Khalilur Rahman, Environment, Forest and Climate Change Minister Abdul Awal Mintoo and State Minister for Foreign Affairs Humaiun Kobir were also present.
Before the opening ceremony, world leaders gathered at the Leaders’ Lounge, where they exchanged greetings and held brief informal conversations on issues of mutual interest.
Tarique also joined the informal interactions in a cordial atmosphere.
Among those who met and exchanged greetings with the prime minister were former Organisation of Islamic Cooperation (OIC) Secretary-General Hissein Brahim Taha, London Mayor Sadiq Khan, Moldovan Prime Minister Vasile Tarlev, Pakistani President Asif Ali Zardari, Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian, Syrian President Ahmed al-Sharaa, Syrian Foreign Minister Asaad al-Shaibani and Kuwaiti Prime Minister Sheikh Ahmad Abdullah Al-Ahmad Al-Sabah.
The prime minister also exchanged greetings with members of the Indonesian delegation.
Heads of state and government, representatives of international organisations and climate experts from different countries are attending COP31, which is focusing on global cooperation to address the challenges of climate change.
Tarique is scheduled to hold bilateral meetings and courtesy calls with the leaders of several countries on the sidelines of the conference.
The prime minister arrived in Antalya on Tuesday on a three-day visit to Türkiye.
Tarique is leading a high-level Bangladesh delegation to the conference.

item.title: Attorney general: Hasina must comply with law if she returns
item.description:
Attorney General Barrister Ruhul Quddus Kazal has said the law is clear on appeals by individuals sentenced to death by the International Crimes Tribunal (ICT), citing a past Supreme Court ruling involving Abdul Kalam Azad.
Speaking to reporters at his Supreme Court office on Wednesday, Kazal said an appeal filed after the prescribed deadline would require the court to consider whether the delay could be condoned.
He said previous statements by government officials and legal representatives on the matter were consistent with the law and involved no misinterpretation.
Referring to the Abdul Kalam Azad case, the attorney general said the Appellate Division had previously considered a request to condone a delayed appeal but did not accept the arguments.
Asked how former prime minister Sheikh Hasina could return to Bangladesh, Kazal said he would not speculate on the process.
“She is a convicted accused sentenced to death and is currently outside Bangladesh. If she wishes to surrender before the law, she may return. But she must comply with the law,” he said.
On November 17, 2025, ICT-1 sentenced Hasina to death in a case involving crimes against humanity committed during the July uprising.
Kazal said any attempt to appeal beyond the stipulated period would be subject to the court’s decision on condoning the delay.

item.title: Madrasa teacher sentenced to death for raping 11-year-old student
item.description:
A Netrokona court has sentenced a madrasa teacher to death for raping an 11-year-old student in Madan upazila of Netrokona, resulting in her pregnancy, reports Bangla Tribune.
The court also fined him Tk1 lakh.
The convict, Aman Ullah Mahmudi, also known as Sagar, was present when the verdict was announced by Judge Abdus Salam of the Netrokona District and Sessions Judge Court at around 1pm on Wednesday. The judge also presides over the Women and Children Repression Prevention Tribunal.
The court had fixed November 11 for the verdict after concluding arguments from the prosecution and defence on October 28. During the hearing, the accused sought acquittal in exchange for transferring ownership of his remaining 12-decimal plot of land, but the court rejected the proposal.
According to the case statement, in November 2025, Aman Ullah Mahmudi, a teacher and director of a women's Qawmi madrasa in Pachhat Barabari village of Kaitail union in Madan upazila, summoned the student to the institution and raped her.
He threatened to kill her if she disclosed the incident. The child remained silent out of fear and eventually stopped attending the madrasa.
Later, her family members became suspicious after noticing physical changes. In April, they took her to a doctor, where it was confirmed that she was pregnant.
On April 23, the victim's mother filed a case with Madan police station, accusing the teacher and his brother, Mamun Mia.
The incident sparked widespread outrage across the country. RAB-14 also launched an investigation. On May 6, the main accused, Sagar, was arrested in Gouripur upazila of Mymensingh. Police later secured a three-day remand to interrogate him.
On July 2, the victim gave birth to a girl at Sylhet MAG Osmani Medical College Hospital.
Following a court order, a Criminal Investigation Department (CID) team collected DNA samples from the newborn and sent them to Dhaka for testing. The report found a 99.99% match between the newborn's DNA and that of the accused teacher.
After receiving the DNA test report, Sub-Inspector Aktaruzzaman, the investigating officer of the case, submitted a charge sheet to the court on August 27, naming Aman Ullah Mahmudi and his brother Mamun Mia as accused.
Arguments from both sides concluded on October 28, when the court fixed November 11 for delivering the verdict.

item.title: TIB condemns state minister's remarks on gifts to engineers, demands withdrawal
item.description:
Transparency International Bangladesh (TIB) has strongly condemned remarks by the state minister for local government, rural development and cooperatives, saying they appear to legitimise bribery under the guise of gifts.
At the inauguration of a training program for newly appointed assistant engineers of the Local Government Engineering Department (LGED) on Tuesday, the state minister reportedly said gifts offered to engineers from contractors' profits after bills are paid promptly, provided work quality is maintained, do not constitute bribes and may be accepted.
TIB questioned whether the remarks effectively legitimise bribery by suggesting that government engineers can receive personal benefits from contractors in return for performing their official duties.
The organisation demanded the immediate withdrawal of the remarks, clarification of the government's position and accountability for both the state minister and the secretary whose advice was reportedly cited in support of the statement.
TIB Executive Director Dr Iftekharuzzaman said verifying work quality, accepting completed projects and ensuring prompt payment of bills in accordance with regulations are routine responsibilities of government engineers.
"Engineers receive salaries and benefits from public funds precisely to perform these duties. Why, then, should they accept illicit payments from contractors under the guise of 'gifts' in return for carrying out their responsibilities?" he said.
He questioned whether the state minister was effectively encouraging the acceptance of bribes by suggesting that engineers could receive gifts for performing their official duties.
Advising newly appointed engineers, whose responsibility is to prevent irregularities in public procurement, to earn money outside the rules from contractors at the outset of their careers was irresponsible and unlawful, he said.
If such remarks are accepted, they could legitimise demands for bribes at the field level and lead to a wider spread of corruption, Iftekharuzzaman added.
He also urged the state minister to identify publicly the law or regulation that permits engineers to receive personal benefits from contractors' profits in exchange for performing their routine duties.
Citing relevant legal provisions, the TIB executive director said Section 161 of the Penal Code makes accepting gratification beyond legally authorised remuneration for performing official duties punishable by law. Section 165 also provides for punishment for accepting valuable items from individuals connected to an official's duties.
He further referred to Rule 5(1) of the Government Servants (Conduct) Rules, 1979, which requires prior government approval, subject to specified exceptions, for accepting gifts that create an obligation towards the donor.
Rule 5(4) sets a Tk500 limit for each gift received by secretaries and officers of equivalent rank from specified sources, while Paragraph 6(2) of Schedule 20 of the Public Procurement Rules, 2025 allows certain low-value promotional items, such as diaries, calendars and pens bearing an organisation's logo, worth up to Tk5,000 per item.
However, neither provision allows engineers to receive personal benefits from contractors as a reward for performing their official duties, he said.
Highlighting the risk of conflicts of interest, Iftekharuzzaman said engineers who accept personal benefits from contractors whose work they supervise may compromise their impartiality.
Such transactions could influence project supervision and bill certification, undermine fair competition among contractors and encourage collusion between engineers and contractors, he added.
He warned that the practice could spread to other government departments, normalising illicit payments under the guise of gifts as a condition for receiving public services.
The TIB executive director also questioned the state minister's reference to advice from a senior secretary.
"If the senior secretary did indeed offer such advice, as described by the state minister, serious questions arise about the secretary's professional integrity and ethical fitness to remain in office," he said.
He also questioned whether there was an attempt to institutionalise collusive corruption between the state minister and the senior secretary, adding that such a position would be embarrassing for the government and the ruling party and contradict the government's election manifesto.
Referring to a previous controversy over the road transport and bridges minister's remarks describing extortion as a matter of negotiated transactions, Iftekharuzzaman said corruption-enabling statements by senior government officials should be treated as warning signs.
TIB called on the state minister to publicly apologise and unconditionally withdraw his remarks. It also urged the government to seek a formal explanation from him, ensure accountability and verify the authenticity of the senior secretary's alleged advice before taking appropriate legal action.

item.title: COP31: Bangladesh seeks easier climate funding, renewable investment
item.description:
Bangladesh is pressing for increased funding to address climate-induced loss and damage, implement adaptation programmes and expand renewable energy at COP31 in Türkiye's Antalya, while raising concerns over the gap between international commitments and their actual implementation.
It is particularly emphasising effective financing to protect the lives and livelihoods of people in coastal areas, haors, chars and drought-prone regions.
Environment, Forest and Climate Change Minister Abdul Awal Mintoo said climate change was causing economic losses of around $15.2 billion annually in Bangladesh.
He said Bangladesh would highlight its position at the conference and push for greater access to international climate funds for countries facing severe climate risks.
The country’s central demand is that climate finance should not add to its debt burden, but instead come through adequate, predictable and easily accessible grants, he said.
For countries like Bangladesh, the effectiveness of a climate conference cannot be measured by declarations and financial pledges alone.
The real test is how much of the promised support reaches vulnerable communities and translates into tangible protection on the ground.
Climate change expert Prof Dr Ainun Nishat believes implementation should be the main focus of this year’s conference, as considerable gaps remain despite political commitments and procedural decisions taken at previous climate summits.
He said establishing funds and financing mechanisms was not enough and effectiveness was needed to be assessed through proper monitoring and evaluation to determine whether the money was being used as intended.
With rising temperatures, natural disasters and climate-related risks expected to intensify, Nishat said climate considerations must be integrated into all development activities rather than being treated as a separate issue.
Bangladeshi climate scientist Dr Atiq Rahman said every country participating in the COP process was a party to the negotiations, and Bangladesh had played an important role in the past as a leading voice of the Least Developed Countries (LDCs).
Although Bangladesh is now in the process of graduating from the LDC category, its experience and role as a former leader and spokesperson of the group remain important in international climate negotiations, he said.
Rahman stressed that attention should not be limited to the decisions reached at the negotiating table; countries must also monitor what changes those decisions bring during implementation.
The growing dependence on loans in Bangladesh’s climate financing has been highlighted in a study by Change Initiative, which raises questions about the sustainability of the country’s transition to renewable energy.
Mofazzal Hossain, research coordinator at the organisation, said loans accounted for 90.4 percent of total investment in Bangladesh’s renewable energy sector since 2000.
According to the research, Bangladesh received a total of $2.54 billion in climate finance for its energy sector. Of this amount, $880 million went to coal- and gas-based power plants, including those at Matarbari and Bheramara.
The study also warns that if the existing financing pattern continues, per capita debt in the renewable energy sector could reach $105 by 2040. Bangladesh’s current per capita climate debt across all sectors stands at around $80.
The organisation has proposed establishing a national financing mechanism titled the ‘Renewable Energy Sovereignty Facility’ to reduce dependence on new public borrowing and expand investment in clean energy.
According to the organisation, the facility could mobilise $7.69 billion in investment in the renewable energy sector between 2026 and 2030.
It could also reduce new government borrowing from $4.6 billion to $800 million.
As a result, per capita debt in the renewable energy sector could fall from $105 to $24 by 2040, representing a reduction of around 77%, the organisation said.
Bangladesh is making grant-based climate finance a central demand at COP31, arguing that vulnerable countries should not have to take on additional debt to address a crisis they have contributed relatively little to creating.
Saimum Parvez, special assistant to the Prime Minister on Environment, Forest and Climate Change, said Bangladesh would strongly raise the need for adequate grant-based financing at the conference.
“Our demand is to increase grants for adaptation and addressing climate-induced losses and damage without adding to the debt burden, and to simplify the application and approval processes for climate funds,” he said.
He said the Bangladesh delegation would coordinate its position with the LDC group, the G77 and other like-minded climate-vulnerable countries to protect the country’s interests.
Several meetings had already been held to coordinate the country’s position, while the Prime Minister would also outline Bangladesh’s priorities in his address, he said.
Bangladeshi experts are also raising various climate-related issues at the conference, Parvez added.
Bangladesh has placed several issues at the centre of its negotiating agenda, with particular emphasis on securing financing without creating further debt.
These include implementing adaptation programmes and the National Adaptation Plan (NAP), securing funds to address climate-induced losses and damage, and making access to the Green Climate Fund easier.
The country is also seeking greater investment in renewable energy, a just transition away from fossil fuels, technology transfer and capacity building.
Other priorities include early warning systems and climate-resilient infrastructure in coastal areas, as well as financial support for non-economic losses such as displacement, loss of livelihoods and damage to cultural heritage.

item.title: Two buses torched in Pallabi
item.description:
Two parked passenger buses belonging to Bikalpa Paribahan and Abhijat Paribahan were set on fire by miscreants in the capital's Pallabi area on Wednesday morning.
The fire damaged the seats, windows and body of one bus, while the rear windowpanes, seats and covers of the other bus were also damaged. No casualties were reported.
The incident took place around Wednesday morning at Phulkali intersection in Section 12 under Pallabi police station.
Police said miscreants arrived on a motorcycle, set fire to the two buses parked on the roadside and fled the scene.
Local residents spotted the flames and managed to bring the fire under control by pouring water on the vehicles.
According to police, the damage to the Bikalpa Paribahan bus is estimated at Tk8 lakh to Tk10 lakh. The damage to the Abhijat Paribahan bus is estimated at around Tk50,000.
Pallabi Police Station Officer-in-Charge (OC) Jalal Uddin said efforts are underway to identify and arrest those involved in the incident.

item.description:

Iftekhar Enam Awal, deputy managing director, Md Arijul Islam Mollick, head of SME Banking, Md Mizanur Rahman, branch manager, Pabna, senior officials of the Bank and local dignitaries were also present at the event.

item.title: Al-Arafah Islami Bank holds leadership development training
item.description:
A daylong training program titled “Connect, Influence & Grow: Leadership Development & Interpersonal Excellence” was held at Al-Arafah Islami Bank Training Institute (AIBTI), aiming to enhance the leadership qualities, interpersonal skills and professional excellence of the Bank’s Senior Executives and Managers.
The program was inaugurated on November 10, Tuesday, by the bank’s managing director Mohd Rafat Ullah Khan, who attended as chief guest.
The session was chaired by principal of AIBTI Md Abdur Rahim Duary.
Mohd Rafat Ullah Khan emphasized that effective leadership, efficient communication, mutual collaboration and accountability are essential for achieving institutional goals in an evolving banking environment.
Alongside professional knowledge, he highlighted the importance of developing leadership qualities, team coordination and the ability to make positive decisions.
He expressed his optimism that such training programs would play a significant role in enhancing both the individual and institutional performance of the Bank’s officials.
The training program was facilitated by Khandaker Zia Hasan, founder and chief executive officer of Zia’s Language Centre, Canada, who attended as resource person.
Through practical discussions and experience-sharing sessions, he presented various strategies for developing leadership skills.
A total of 40 Senior Executives and Managers of the Bank participated in the training program.
The day-long session covered various aspects of leadership concepts and development, emotional intelligence, communication skills, interpersonal relationship building, fostering mutual trust and enhancing team effectiveness.
These competencies are expected to contribute to improved workplace performance and enhanced customer service.

item.title: Community Bank extends Tk1.3cr CSR support to Bangladesh Police Institutions
item.description:
Community Bank Bangladesh PLC has provided Tk1.30 crore from its CSR fund to three Bangladesh Police institutions to support healthcare, education and childcare.
The bank allocated Tk1 crore to APBN Medical Center in Uttara, Dhaka, to strengthen its healthcare services and Tk20 lakh to APBN School in Uttara to support its educational programs.
APBN Day-Care Center received Tk10 lakh to improve its facilities.
Md Ali Hossain Fakir, Inspector General of Police and chairman of Community Bank Bangladesh PLC, handed over the cheques alongside Mohammed Emtiaz Uddin, the bank’s managing director.
The heads of the three institutions received the cheques in the presence of senior officials from Bangladesh Police and the bank.
Under the leadership of its managing director, Community Bank continues to advance its commitment to social development and public welfare by strengthening institutions that expand opportunities for children and provide essential services to families.

item.title: Trends Bird, East West Chemicals sign strategic MoU
item.description:
Trends Bird Limited (TBL) and East West Chemicals Limited (EWCL) have recently signed a significant Memorandum of Understanding (MoU), marking the beginning of a strategic collaboration aimed at developing and implementing a customized Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) system for EWCL.
Under the collaboration, Trends Bird Limited will design, develop, implement, deploy and hand over a customized Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) system for East West Chemicals Limited.
The system is intended to bring EWCL's major operational, commercial, financial and management processes together on one platform, replacing separate working methods with a connected, data-driven approach.
The ERP will cover key areas of EWCL's business, including procurement and inventory, import and LC management, quality control, batch and expiry management, depot and distribution management, sales, delivery and collection, finance and accounts, audit and management controls, and HR and field force functions.
The collaboration reflects a shared vision of strengthening EWCL's digital capability and building a lasting working relationship between the two companies.

item.title: Act early, Live life Shukhee
item.description:
Millions of people in Bangladesh live with diabetes without knowing it, and many discover it only when complications have already reached their eyes, kidneys, heart or feet. Yet with early screening, timely care and simple changes in daily life, diabetes can be prevented, delayed and managed well. To mark World Diabetes Day under the global theme "Early action on diabetes", Grameen HealthTech Limited (Shukhee), in partnership with Experto ReWell, hosted a seminar titled "Act Early, Live Life Shukhee" on 10 November 2026 at Telecom Bhaban.
Mohammad Solaimun Rasel, CTO and CBO of GHL, inaugurated the session. Md. Ashraful Hassan, Chairman, Grameen Group, attended as Chief Guest. He said, "Grameen's journey began with a belief in standing beside people. Today, that same belief is carrying us to the doorstep of healthcare. Through our eye hospitals, a person regains their sight; through safe sanitation, a family gets the foundation of a healthy life; and through digital initiatives like Shukhee, even people in remote villages receive quality medical care. We believe that only healthy people can build a prosperous society. Our commitment is to bring healthcare to every person through the power of social business." Dr. Ahmed Armaan Siddiqui, Chief Executive Officer of GHL/Shukhee, shared his vision of one ecosystem with a shared preventive health mission, from screening to measurable health outcomes. Mohammad Moinul Hakim, CEO of Experto ReWell, presented EverGreen Health™, LinX CGM and Whole-Body Digital Twin technology, showing how screening can lead to precision prevention.
An expert session was conducted by Prof. Dr. Md. Robed Amin, Professor of Medicine, Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, Prof. Dr. Md. Feroz Amin, Director, BIRDEM, Dr. Hurjahan Banu (Urmi), Associate Professor of Endocrinology and Metabolism, Bangladesh Medical University. Also present were Brig Gen Dr. Md. Jalal Uddin (Retd), Advisor to the Chairman, Grameen Telecom Trust and other high officials.

item.title: E-CAB election tensions escalate amid obstruction and assault allegations
item.description:
Tensions have escalated ahead of the December 19 E-Commerce Association of Bangladesh (E-CAB) election, with candidates alleging physical assaults, intimidation and attempts to prevent them from collecting nomination papers.
In the latest incident on Wednesday, Hosne Ara Nuri, also known as Nowrin, a candidate for the post of general secretary, was taken to Dhanmondi West Police Station by a group of people after she went to the association's office in Dhanmondi to collect her nomination paper.
Videos of the incident have circulated on social media, showing a group of people surrounding her and taking her to the police station.
Nowrin had obtained police clearance on November 9 and deposited Tk1 lakh with E-CAB on November 10 as part of the election process.
Hours before the incident, Nowrin had told the media that she felt unsafe while attempting to participate in the election.
She alleged that followers of Kazi Mukituzzaman Mukit, who is reportedly associated with Jubo Dal, and a few others had been gathering near the E-CAB office throughout the day, creating an intimidating environment.
"Ordinary E-CAB members want the organization’s leadership to be elected through voting in a festive atmosphere. However, followers of Kazi Mukituzzaman Mukit and a few others, including people associated with Jubo Dal, have been sitting near the E-CAB office with groups of people throughout the day, creating disorder. On Tuesday, Mukit's followers tore up the nomination paper of a presidential candidate. Now I am also afraid to collect my nomination paper," she said.
A few hours later, when she went to collect her nomination paper, a group of people allegedly labelled her a collaborator of the previous authoritarian regime and took her to the police station.
Several E-CAB members have alleged that Mukit was behind the incident. However, the allegation could not be independently verified.
An E-CAB member, speaking on condition of anonymity, said Nowrin was a popular candidate and that the incident appeared to be an attempt to prevent her from contesting by delaying the collection of her nomination paper until the deadline passed.
The latest incident came a day after another candidate's representative alleged that he was assaulted and his nomination paper torn up at the E-CAB office on Tuesday, November 10.
However, nomination papers can be collected until November 12, 2026.
According to a written complaint sent by email to Dhanmondi police, the complainant, Mohammad Kawsar Jahan, head of HR and administration at Labaid Cancer Hospital, said he had collected a nomination paper on behalf of Labaid Group Managing Director Sakif Shamiim, who intends to contest the post of president.
He alleged that shortly after leaving the office at around 3:30pm, a group of people attacked and physically assaulted him before tearing up the nomination paper.
He described the incident as an attempt by an interested group to obstruct the upcoming 2026-28 election and undermine a democratic and competitive electoral process.
An E-CAB member alleged that the incident was linked to efforts to prevent Shamiim from contesting. He also claimed that Jannatul Shapla, wife of Narsingdi-5 MP Engineer Ashraf Uddin Bakul, intends to contest the presidential post.
The member further alleged that some individuals had informally formed a panel and were attempting to secure positions without facing competition. E-CAB has no officially announced panel for this year's election.
Contacted over Wednesday's incident, Dhanmondi police station Officer-in-Charge Imdadul Islam Tayeb said Nowrin had been kept at the station for her own safety.
"We have checked everything and found nothing against her. Considering the situation, we will release her shortly," he said.
Asked what measures E-CAB would take to ensure candidates' safety and an inclusive election, Election Committee Chairman Mustafiz said the committee was not responsible for such matters.
"Our responsibility is limited to preparing the voter list and organising the election. Who contests and who does not is not my concern. The E-CAB administrator will look into these matters," he said.
However, when contacted, E-CAB Administrator Sharif Mustafiz said the matter fell under the responsibility of the election commission chairman.
Neither the election committee chairman nor the administrator provided a clear account of what measures would be taken to prevent further incidents and ensure a safe environment for candidates.

item.title: Students caught between digital learning and screen addiction
item.description:
Smartphones are increasingly accessible to students, from secondary school to even primary school, offering access to online classes, information and educational content. However, growing use of social media, online games and entertainment has raised concerns about addiction, declining concentration, sleep disruption and risks to physical and mental health.
The debate now centres on how to balance the educational benefits of technology with the need to protect children through age-based guidelines, parental supervision and institutional oversight.
According to the Bangladesh Bureau of Statistics (BBS) ICT Usage and Application Survey for the April-June quarter of FY2025-26, 89.6% of people aged five and above use mobile phones, up from 88.2% in the same period a year earlier. Smartphone use stood at 75.1%, while 65.6% of people owned a mobile phone. Nearly 99% of households had access to mobile phones.
Internet use among people aged five and above stood at 59.2%, compared with 55% a year earlier. However, only 58.2% of households had internet connections, highlighting the digital divide between access to devices and connectivity.
There are no recent nationwide figures on personal mobile phone use among primary and secondary school students. A 2021 study published in an international journal's Health Science Reports , based on 1,803 secondary school students across 21 districts, found that 67.11% used mobile phones daily. The study, which drew on 2020 data, also linked device use to headaches, back pain, vision problems and sleep disturbances.
Smartphones can help students access online lessons, educational videos, information and language-learning resources, particularly in remote areas. However, excessive use can eat into study time, disrupt sleep and discourage physical activity and outdoor play.
Psychiatrist Dr Mekhla Sarkar said smartphones are designed to encourage prolonged use, making children and adolescents particularly vulnerable to addiction.
Warning signs include steadily increasing screen time, declining academic performance, reduced interest in sports, strained family and peer relationships, and irregular sleeping and eating habits, she said.
Sarkar warned that excessive smartphone use could affect children's physical development, increase the risk of obesity and eye problems, and undermine their social skills. Spending too much time in virtual environments could also make it harder for children to develop realistic expectations and cope with challenges in everyday life.
The Directorate of Secondary and Higher Education (DSHE) issued a directive in October 2017 restricting the use of mobile phones by students and teachers in classrooms. However, questions remain over its implementation.
DSHE Director General Prof Dr Khan Moinuddin Al Mahmud Sohel said a complete ban on mobile phones was not practical, but students should not have unrestricted access to them. He said discussions had taken place on formulating guidelines to prevent addiction and help students focus on their studies.
Education Minister Dr ANM Ehsanul Hoque Milon and State Minister for Primary and Mass Education Bobby Hajjaj have also called for responsible parental supervision and coordinated efforts involving families, schools and communities.
Educationist Rasheda K Chowdhury said restrictions must extend beyond schools to homes, with parents playing an active role. She called for blocking harmful content and providing children with opportunities to participate in sports, storytelling, art and other creative activities.
Cybersecurity expert Arif Moinuddin recommended strict controls on smartphone use during class hours, along with screen-time limits and more extracurricular activities, including debates, sports, science clubs and technology fairs.
Education researcher KM Enamul Haque said a blanket ban would overlook the growing role of digital devices in education. Instead, he suggested introducing age- and institution-specific rules that clearly define when, where and why students may use smartphones and other devices.
Education stakeholders say a coordinated approach combining age-based national guidelines, parental supervision, school-level rules and alternative activities is needed to ensure that children use technology safely and for educational purposes.

item.title: Mir Mugdho memorial defaced again in Brahmanbaria
item.description:
A memorial dedicated to July uprising martyr Mir Mugdho in Chinair of Brahmanbaria Sadar upazila has been defaced with black paint again, obscuring much of his portrait and name.
Local resident and Jubo Dal leader Md Uzzal Ahmed confirmed the incident. He said he noticed the defacement on Wednesday afternoon, adding that the memorial had been similarly defaced before.
Ripan Das, inspector (investigation) of Brahmanbaria Sadar Police Station, said police visited the site after receiving reports of the incident.
He said police were investigating how the memorial was defaced and who was responsible.
On November 25, 2025, the memorial in Chinair was similarly defaced with black paint. However, those responsible for that incident were never identified.

item.title: Four-star Bangladesh down Sri Lanka to finish as group winners
item.description:
Hamza Choudhury, Shamit Shome, Farhaan Ali Wahid and Rakib Hossain scored a goal each as Bangladesh produced a commanding 4-0 victory over Sri Lanka in their second and final Group A fixture at the National Stadium, Dhaka on Wednesday.
With two wins from as many matches, the men in red and green, who had already secured a semi-final berth before the match, finished the group stage as leaders.
Bangladesh head coach Thomas Dooley made three changes to the starting XI, handing Hamza and Farhaan their first starts of the tournament after the two late arrivals joined the national team ahead of the Sri Lanka fixture.
Faisal Fahim and Jamal Bhuiyan were left out, while the third change saw Mohammad Ibrahim replace Bishwanath Ghosh, who picked up an injury during training the day after Bangladesh's 1-0 victory over Bhutan.
Bangladesh put Sri Lanka under pressure from the outset, with Hamza's free-kick in the sixth minute sailing over the crossbar after Rakib earned a set-piece opportunity just outside the box.
Shamit broke the deadlock two minutes later with a volley from the edge of the box after Sri Lankan goalkeeper Sujan Perera punched away Hamza's cross. Shamit's initial volley was blocked by the defence, but the midfielder made no mistake with his second attempt.
Hamza showcased his impressive technique in the 25th minute with a spectacular backheel effort that narrowly missed the target. A quick move down the left flank ended with Shamit heading a long ball into Hamza's path. The Leicester City midfielder beat the advancing goalkeeper to the ball but, with little time to react, attempted a backheel that went just wide.
Shamit tested Perera again in the 42nd minute with a low effort from around 20 yards, but the goalkeeper produced a diving save.
Hamza started as the attacking midfielder behind Ibrahim but frequently switched positions with the striker, who also drifted to the left, allowing Hamza to operate as the central striker at times.
The Leicester City midfielder doubled Bangladesh's lead in the 44th minute. Receiving a through ball from Ibrahim, Hamza surged into the box before beating the goalkeeper with a fiery finish.
Farhaan produced arguably the most eye-catching moment of the match to score Bangladesh's third goal seven minutes into the second half.
The UK-based winger drove into the box from the left, danced past two defenders, beat another with his dribbling skills and capped the brilliant solo run with a clinical finish.
Rakib put the result beyond doubt in the 87th minute with another fine finish to complete Bangladesh's four-goal rout.
Bangladesh will face Pakistan in the second semi-final on Saturday, following the first last-four clash between India and Bhutan at the same venue.
